headline: Highest risk is Devin’s broad write/network/OAuth access; Marker is read-only, so pairwise prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict risks are mostly bounded and compliance risk is low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can ingest files, browser content, and MCP outputs, while marker has no write or MCP surface and no documented shared channel. A prompt-injection pathway is therefore not default; it would require manual copy/paste or an external bridge. The blast radius is limited because marker is read-only.
conditions: IF an operator copies marker-generated text into Devin’s prompt or MCP input, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the pathway opens.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy/paste of untrusted marker output into Devin prompts.
Require a human review step before Devin consumes any marker-produced text.
Use provenance labels on any shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or structured-output parsing for cross-agent handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and integration tokens, but marker has no filesystem read, network egress, or documented data sink. With no shared workspace or outbound channel on marker, leakage from Devin to marker is not default and is limited to whatever a human manually transfers.
conditions: IF a shared workspace is introduced, Devin’s files could be exposed to marker.
IF an operator pastes Devin outputs containing secrets into marker, those secrets are disclosed.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in shared documents.
Use separate repositories or folders per agent.
Redact tokens before handing text to marker.
Restrict Devin’s access to least-privilege integrations.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on cross-agent artifact transfer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has broad write and git capabilities, but marker has no filesystem write, git, or network capabilities, so there is no overlapping mutable resource to contend over. The pair lacks a plausible write-write conflict pathway in the provided profiles.
conditions: IF marker is later given write access to the same repo or workspace, conflict risk appears.
IF an orchestrator grants both agents concurrent git writes, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Keep marker read-only.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repo by Devin and any future writer.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
Require lockfiles or PR-based handoff for writes.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking if marker gains write access.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin can autonomously act on browser, shell, and integration outputs, while marker is a document processor that may produce text Devin could treat as authoritative. Because the profiles do not document a verification step between them, a bad extraction from marker can cascade into Devin’s actions in default handoffs.
conditions: IF Devin consumes marker output without human or programmatic verification, errors can propagate.
IF marker extracts a document incorrectly and Devin uses it for code or ticket actions, downstream mistakes occur.
mitigations: Require a verification step before Devin acts on marker output.
Use schema-validated handoff formats.
Have Devin cite source passages before taking action.
Limit marker output to extracted fields, not free text.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks between extraction and action.

E_compliance.rationale: Devin handles source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and integration tokens, but marker’s profile shows no touched data classes, residency, or retention obligations. With no documented compliance mismatch between the pair, only a small residual risk remains from manual transfer of regulated content.
conditions: IF regulated data is manually copied from Devin into marker, compliance obligations may attach.
IF marker is deployed with a different retention policy than Devin, mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to marker.
Document retention rules for any shared artifacts.
Use separate access controls for Devin and marker.
Review whether any transferred docs contain personal data.
requires-engineering: formalize residency and retention policy mapping.
